forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 25%. Past 24 hours: no AGI declaration from any lab. Air Street's State of AI: May 2026 release reiterates that both Anthropic's Claude Mythos and OpenAI's GPT-5.5 cleared UK AISI's 32-step 'Last Ones' cyber-attack simulation only 3/10 runs — strong capability signal but well short of an AGI claim. SpaceX-Anthropic data-centre deal (May 6) extends compute lock-in for the 2027-28 capability bow-wave. Amodei reiterated 2027 timeline at Davos in January. Resolution window remains ~32 months; no shift in the underlying drivers, hence hold.
forecasts.base_rate: ~22-25% aggregated from Metaculus (~25% by 2029), Kalshi (~40% OpenAI-specific by 2030) and superforecaster surveys
factors_up: Anthropic-SpaceX data centre deal May 6 deepens compute moat (+1pp)
Air Street State of AI May 2026 confirms continued benchmark gains (+1pp)
Amodei January Davos comments maintaining ~2027 timeline (+1pp)
OpenAI $122B funding round with $35B AGI/IPO contingency keeps declaration incentive live (+1pp)
factors_down: AISI cyber-attack benchmark passed only 3/10 by frontier models — capability still uneven (-2pp)
Resolution requires explicit lab declaration or 3+ researcher endorsement (-2pp)
Resolution window now ~32 months — time decay (-1pp)
CAISI pre-deployment regime extended to all big labs May 5 raises declaration friction (-1pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether the Anthropic-OpenAI accounting dispute spills into AGI claims as a marketing lever
Whether a Mythos-class or GPT-6 release in H2 2026 prompts a formal declaration
How the Trump-administration NIST/CAISI regime treats unilateral AGI claims

update_triggers.up: A frontier lab publicly declares AGI; or 3+ leading researchers publicly endorse achieved status
update_triggers.down: Capability plateau at next-gen frontier; major lab walks back AGI timeline; CAISI imposes formal pre-disclosure delay

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Up 1pp to 25%. Fresh Finalround AI / Yahoo coverage (May 2026) reports McKinsey now planning ~10% global headcount reduction over next 18 months explicitly attributed to AI agent deployment, on top of the ~200 tech/support cuts confirmed in late 2025 and the 5,000-headcount reduction over five years. Inc/Fast Company frame the cuts as a 'warning signal' for the industry. Separate McKinsey survey reports 30% of companies plan AI-related layoffs in 2026. Still far short of a ≥33% sector-wide decline from 2024 baseline, but the trajectory and the share of credible commentary attributing it to AI keep nudging the estimate up.
forecasts.base_rate: ~20% sector-wide ≥33% disruption within 6 years for any AI-exposed white-collar industry
factors_up: McKinsey 10% planned reduction tied explicitly to AI agents (+3pp)
30% of firms in 2026 McKinsey survey plan AI-driven layoffs (+1pp)
Inc/Fast Company framing cuts as industry warning signal (+1pp)
Entry-level consulting postings now demanding AI fluency — pyramid economics under strain (+1pp)
factors_down: Cuts so far concentrated in tech/support roles, not client-facing consultants (-2pp)
Big 4 / Accenture revenue still growing on AI advisory work (-2pp)
≥33% decline in revenue OR employment is a very high bar by end-2030 (-2pp)
Resolution requires 2+ credible analyses primarily attributing decline to AI — high evidentiary threshold (-1pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether AI agent deployment cannibalises strategy work or expands it
How Big 4 vs MBB differential plays out — Accenture/Deloitte may absorb share
Whether the 'consultancy revenue' baseline includes AI-implementation work

update_triggers.up: Major firm announces >20% headcount cut; first credible analyst report estimating sector revenue down >15% YoY attributed to AI
update_triggers.down: MBB firms confirm AI-driven margin expansion without revenue decline; sector revenue grows YoY 2026

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: Up 1pp to 2%. Local elections on 7 May 2026 confirmed scale of Labour's collapse: lost 1,496 councillors and 38 councils; Reform UK gained 1,453 seats and 14 councils including first London authority (Havering) and Sunderland. Starmer rejecting calls to resign, framing as '10-year project'. YouGov 4-5 May voting intention: Reform 25%, Lab 18%, Con 17%, Grn 15%, LD 14% — Labour third behind Reform and arguably losing to Conservatives at the seat-conversion level under uniform swing. The small uptick (1→2pp) reflects that election deadline is still by Dec 2029 (>3.5 years) and political volatility is genuinely high (Reform also untested in government); but Labour-largest scenarios remain a long-tail recovery story.
forecasts.base_rate: ~5-10% for a governing party 3+ years out polling third with this scale of local-election rout to recover to largest party
factors_up: 3.5+ years until deadline allows time for recovery (+2pp)
Reform UK untested in coalitions and governance — could lose support if errors emerge (+1pp)
First-past-the-post still rewards efficient vote distribution; Labour retains incumbent infrastructure (+1pp)
factors_down: Local elections showed historic 1,496-seat loss, 38 councils lost (-3pp)
YouGov has Labour third at 18%, behind Reform 25% and effectively tied with Con 17% (-2pp)
Internal calls for Starmer to resign signal party disunity (-2pp)
Reform-Conservative voter migration patterns make Labour pluralities harder under FPTP (-1pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether Starmer survives leadership challenge in next 12 months
How Reform-Conservative competition splits the right-wing vote
Whether economic conditions improve materially before 2029

update_triggers.up: Reform fragments or hits governance scandal; Labour polls return to 25%+; Starmer replaced and party rebounds
update_triggers.down: Starmer resigns and party splits; Reform-Con pact forms; Labour polling falls into single digits

forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 76%. The 8.5-year window absorbs most short-term noise. Air Street State of AI May 2026 and AGI Timelines Dashboard (Goodheart Labs) show median forecaster timeline at ~2031, well within 2035. LessWrong visualisation: every cohort updating Jan-Apr 2026 moved their AGI timeline earlier. Aimultiple aggregate of 9,800 predictions clusters around late-2020s/early-2030s. SpaceX-Anthropic deal, Mythos and GPT-5.5 capability gains all reinforce the trajectory but were already priced in. Probability that *no* lab declares AGI within ~104 months remains low given current compute scaling and capability slopes.
forecasts.base_rate: ~70-80% aggregated from Metaculus median (~2033), Goodheart Labs dashboard (2031, 80% CI 2027-2045), aimultiple analysis
factors_up: Metaculus / Goodheart aggregate median ~2031 — comfortably inside window (+3pp)
Jan-Apr 2026 cohort updates all moved AGI timelines earlier (+2pp)

Cyber-attack and agentic benchmark passes reinforce trajectory (+1pp)
factors_down: Resolution still requires explicit declaration or 3+ researcher endorsement (-3pp)
Possible scaling plateau between 2028 and 2032 (-2pp)
Regulatory friction (CAISI, EU AI Act, possible Chinese restrictions) could delay declaration (-2pp)

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 8%. AEI China & Taiwan Updates (May 1 and May 8) show continued grey-zone pressure but no kinetic escalation. Trump-Xi summit reportedly scheduled for May in Beijing — could either de-escalate (deal) or escalate (collapse) but the modal outcome is dialogue rather than action. US arms package to Taiwan ($11B Dec 2025, $14B under consideration) increases the cost of Chinese action without changing immediate probability. Defense Priorities and Stimson analyses continue to argue invasion is unlikely; analyst commentary increasingly focused on blockade rather than full invasion. Window is now ~44 months. Hold.

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 1%. ONS March 2026 release (22 April) showed CPI at 3.3%, UP from 3.0% in February — inflation trajectory is moving away from target, not toward it. Transport division up 4.7% YoY (highest since Dec 2022); services 4.5%. April 2026 data due 20 May; consensus expects further upside given energy/transport pressures. BoE April 2026 Monetary Policy Report has not signalled a path to <2% within 2026. With only ~8 months left for a sub-2% print, would require an unprecedented collapse — implausible from a 3.3% base in any base-effect scenario. Hold at floor.
forecasts.base_rate: <5% probability of >1.3pp single-month drop from current base in 8 months absent recession
factors_up: Possible recession could trigger demand collapse (+1pp)
Energy price collapse remains tail scenario (+1pp)
factors_down: March 2026 CPI 3.3%, UP from 3.0% February (-3pp)
Transport inflation 4.7% — highest since Dec 2022 (-1pp)
Core inflation 3.1%, services 4.5% — sticky components (-1pp)
Only ~8 months remain for a sub-2% print (-2pp)
BoE April MPR has not signalled <2% path in 2026 (-1pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether April 2026 print (20 May) shows a downside surprise
How energy markets evolve through summer 2026
Whether any major recession materialises in H2 2026

update_triggers.up: Major energy-price collapse; CPI surprises down 1pp+ in single month; BoE signals undershoot
update_triggers.down: Further CPI upside; services inflation accelerates

forecasts.key_change: Hold at 98%. Variety (May 2026) confirms 31 July 2026 US release, positioning the film for the full late-summer/autumn window plus pre-holiday play. forecasts.question: Will OpenAI and Anthropic have a combined ARR exceeding $70B by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 99%. The AI Corner / SaaStr / Sacra reporting (April-May 2026) puts Anthropic at ~$30B ARR (April 2026, up from $9B in February — 3x in 4 months) and OpenAI at ~$24B in April 2026. Combined gross ~$54B. OpenAI's internal memo (13 April) disputes Anthropic's number and would put it at ~$22B net, making combined ~$46B. Even on the conservative accounting, with Anthropic doubling Q-over-Q and OpenAI growing strongly, combined Q4 2026 ARR comfortably exceeds $70B on virtually any reasonable trajectory. Resolution risk is now almost entirely about which accounting convention the resolver applies; both companies' Q4 disclosures will likely meet the threshold. Hold near ceiling.

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: Down 1pp to 40%. OBR March 2026 EFO assumes medium-term productivity growth picking up to ~1% with labour-supply growth declining to ~0.5% by 2030 — implying real GDP growth of ~1.4-1.5%, just at the threshold. OBR explicitly flags upside scenario at 1.5% productivity (driven by AI) and downside at 0.5%. IPPR commentary urges OBR to hold its nerve on productivity. With Reform UK surging and Labour government weakened by May local elections, policy continuity risk is elevated — political turbulence ahead of late-2029 election adds downside without symmetric upside. Slight downgrade.
forecasts.base_rate: ~30-40% for UK to exceed 1.5% real GDP growth average over a decade given pre-2024 trend ~1.4%
factors_up: OBR upside scenario (AI-driven 1.5% productivity) plausible if Anthropic/OpenAI deploy widely (+2pp)

factors_down: OBR central case implies ~1.4-1.5% — right at threshold (-2pp)
Reform-led political turbulence elevates fiscal/policy uncertainty (-2pp)
Population ageing pulls labour supply growth to ~0.5% by 2030 (-1pp)
Post-financial-crisis productivity trend has been ~0.5% — momentum is unfavourable (-1pp)
